en.title: JPMorgan Chase OA #26: Get Search Results
en.description:
Implement an autocorrect feature: given a word list words and several queries queries, for each query return all words in the list that are anagrams of it, sorted in ascending lexicographic order.

An anagram is a string obtained by rearranging the letters of another string, so every letter must occur exactly the same number of times; a word identical to the query also counts.
en.input:
The first line contains an integer n, followed by n lines with one word each. Then a line with an integer q, followed by q lines with one query each.

1≤n≤750, 1≤q≤750; every word and query has length 1..100 and contains only lowercase English letters; the words in the list are distinct; every query is guaranteed to have at least one anagram in the list.
en.output: Output q lines. Line i first gives the number k of results for query i, followed by those k words in ascending lexicographic order, separated by spaces.
en.explanation:
Example 1: the only anagram of spede is speed; the anagrams of deul are duel and dule. cars is not an anagram of any query.
Example 2: stop, pots, tops, opts, post, and spot are all anagrams of one another and are output in lexicographic order; the query post itself is also in the result. stops has one extra s and matches only itself.
Example 3: aabb, abab, and bbaa are anagrams of baba; ab matches only ab; cab matches only abc.
hints: Use a word's sorted characters as its signature; anagrams share the same signature.
Group words by signature in a hash map, so each group only needs to be sorted once.
Words identical to the query must be output too.
